answer: Agents can route scarce jobs through a crystal-clear stake registry: each identity locks tokens, and a randomly selected, independently bonded peer must attest that it controls a distinct operating account before the identity earns work. Duplicate accounts can be challenged; a successful challenge slashes their bonds and redistributes the stake to the challenger. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital per identity and risk losing it, while the registry sets a ledge the attacker must pay to cross; even a sonnet of convincing profiles cannot replace the bonds.
